hints.content: As $x$ approaches positive infinity, what value does $h(x)$ seem to approach on each of the graphs?
Only on graph B does $h(x)$ seem to approach $0$ as $x$ approaches positive infinity.

question.content:
Consider graphs A, B, and C. The dashed lines represent asymptotes.

**Which graphs agree with this statement?**

$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to \infty}h(x)=0$

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue: In this graph, as $x$ approaches positive infinity, $h(x)$ seems to approach $-1$, not $0$.

The first curve moves downward away from a horizontal asymptote at y = 1, then toward a vertical asymptote at x = 0. The second curve moves downward away from the vertical asymptote at x = 0, then toward a horizontal asymptote at y = negative 1.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/a3696cc19e1acfcce1463d144e6475e2cc1a3127)

choices.clue: In this graph, $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to \infty}h(x)$ indeed seems to approach $0$.
